title: Prepare Linux systemd lifecycle observation script

findings.failure: kizuki serve stop sends SIGTERM. Unit Restart=on-failure does not restart SIGTERM. systemctl then reports is-enabled enabled/0 and is-active inactive/3. query() maps that to state=disabled with enabled=true. changeService requires confirmedActive (active&&enabled) or confirmedStopped (!enabled && disabled|absent|masked), so serve --install and serve --uninstall both throw 'service state is unknown or inconsistent; no service change made'.
findings.affected_invariant: docs/service-lifecycle.md: uninstall must be able to confirm stop+disable and must not delete vault data; stop is documented as a termination request, not removal, but it can block the public uninstall path.
findings.evidence: Static source trace. Independent expected behavior encoded in expected-observations.json and observe-linux-systemd-lifecycle.sh steps install_after_stop / uninstall_after_stop. Not observed on a real systemd user manager.
findings.smallest_correction: Allow uninstall (disable --now) from enabled+inactive, or map that pair to a state uninstall can confirm, or document and recover via systemctl --user start before further CLI mutations. Do not weaken confirmedActive for install.

findings.failure: RFC 0002 §11.1 says systemctl --user enable --now plus loginctl enable-linger guidance. Current enable() runs daemon-reload, enable, restart and never prints or invokes linger.
findings.affected_invariant: No-fake-surface / documentation accuracy. P006 owns canonical docs; this packet does not rewrite them.
findings.evidence: grep loginctl in /repo hits only the RFC.
